tells: A specific, witty concept, a 'Blanc Voyeur Club' about peeping and desire. Hands made into binoculars, 'Melones' innuendo and a tongue all build one cheeky narrative

tells: Voronoi tessellation is the one visual system throughout, and it is used to build things: dense cell clusters gather into a face and break apart again, so the effect has a subject

Frames vary a lot: dark ground with sparse cells, an inverted light frame with stretched horizontal bands, a profile coming out of particles, a rectangular void framed by striations, then a frontal face reveal. That reads as real choreography of cell density over time
Cell scale and density are varied on purpose to model form (fine cells for features, coarse cells for the ground), which shows control rather than a stock plugin preset
No type is visible. Its absence suits a purely graphic, audio-reactive piece
Strictly greyscale with flat gradient grounds. It is coherent but austere, and some frames look like a generative sketch rather than a finished image
gaps: Add a deliberate palette or a single tonal shift at key moments. Pure greyscale on gradient grounds caps how memorable the frames are next to C's colour authority
Give the face (the emotional subject) more material and light, such as depth, shading inside the cells or a light source, so it is not a white blob on a flat field
Raise the piece above a generative technique demo with a clearer concept or narrative arc. The Voronoi effect risks being the whole idea

tells: Photogrammetry and point-cloud capture of real streets is deliberately broken: inverted red architecture, cloud-sky geometry that has melted into black shards, a kaleidoscopic tower of houses seen from below against a fire-lit sky
Every frame has a different spatial logic, which implies real camera choreography through a scanned world and a deliberate aesthetic of datamosh and mesh failure
Type is integrated into space: a text corpus is mapped onto building surfaces in a monospace face, and it reads as a concept (theory, simulation, MIDI) rather than slide text
The palette is unusual and committed (saturated oxblood red against acid yellow and teal), not a default accent
Craft deliberately looks rough and glitchy, and some frames are muddy rather than designed posters
gaps: Tighten frame-level composition. Several frames are visually noisy without a clear focal point, while C makes every frame a poster
Give the projected typography more typographic intent (scale contrast, hierarchy, a chosen face beyond default monospace) so it carries the idea rather than texture
Control the glitch artefacts so the degradation reads as authored rather than accidental, especially in the shard and mesh frame

gaps: The neon finale could push light further (bloom, reflection, flicker artefacts) to match the richness of the daytime frames
Some frames depend on a familiar contemporary flat-illustration vocabulary, and a more unexpected shape language would raise originality further
Show more evidence of camera and depth play between scenes (parallax, layered reveals) to lift the inferred motion beyond cut-to-cut

defects: Two of six sampled frames (the opening water plate and the near-black 4th frame) are effectively empty: more than 1 s of dead air with no subject
'TO STAY' is cut off at the bottom by the horizon/frame edge, and in the second frame of the pair a hard light line slices through it, so the payoff word is unreadable
The dark 'WE WERE NEVER MEANT TO STAY' type is very low-contrast against the grey starfield and reads as muddy rather than as a deliberate blackout
Words appear by hard pops ('LOW' → 'LOW TIDE') with no build of light, no bulb warm-up and no stagger
The letter going out in 'HARBOUR' is a smeared block-dim, not individual bulbs failing, so the idea is under-built
At 100% the bulbs show directional motion-smear and zig-zag jitter that looks like a noisy displacement filter rather than lens-blurred light; the glow has little bloom falloff
The water plate is a horizontally stretched blur texture with no specular glints responding to the lights above
Spectrogram shows a broadband click/spike at ~13.0 s and a full-band dropout/gap at ~15.8 s, which read as edit artefacts, not designed hits
Shots run 7–8 s with only word-on events inside them; the camera, light and water are essentially static
gaps: Motion: there is no choreography in the bulbs themselves. Top work would have bulbs flicker on in sequence, fail one by one on 'lights are gone' and pulse with the tide, and would move the camera or the reflections so each 7 s shot carries motion instead of word pops

Finish: the light is not convincing as light. It needs real bloom and halation, warm-to-cool falloff, clean bulb point sources instead of jittery smears, reflections that ripple coherently in the water, and type kept inside safe area

Sound and structure: one continuous pad/piano bed with a single entry at ~2.9 s, flat dynamics and no designed sound for bulbs igniting or dying. Picture events don't land on transients, there are stray click and gap artefacts, and the energy dips into a dark middle without building to a peak before the warm 'ON' release
